title: Implement Permissions for Blog Posts
description: Add permissions to control who can edit and delete posts, and enforce them in views.
problemStatement:
## Your Mission

Assume you have a `Post` model with `author` (ForeignKey to User).

1. Create a group called `Editors` and give it the `change_post` permission.
2. In the view that edits a post, ensure the user has either the `change_post` permission OR is the author of the post.
3. In the view that deletes a post, ensure the user has the `delete_post` permission.
4. In templates, show/hide edit/delete buttons based on these permissions.

Use the `@permission_required` decorator where appropriate, and combine with custom logic in the view for the author check.
hints: For the author check, you may need to bypass the permission decorator and write a custom check in the view.
To show/hide buttons in template, use `{% if perms.blog.change_post or post.author == user %}`.
expectedOutput: Only editors or the post author can edit; only users with delete permission can delete. Buttons appear accordingly.
